segments.content:
Chapter 106 Shameless Campus Promotion (Bonus chapter for Alliance Leader cry疯子)

The New Sun Student Center did not yet exist in 2004.

At this time, Peking University's various clubs held their activities mainly at the old student activity center, as well as near the Second Teaching Building and the May Fourth athletic field.

Saturday, north side of the May Fourth athletic field.

There were a few badminton courts inside the gymnasium, but they were temporary, marked out on shared space with the basketball and volleyball courts.

The badminton association had applied for the courts in advance and was currently conducting technical skills training.

Chen Guiliang came in carrying several boxes of *Sanguosha*, stood by the side, and watched for a few minutes, carefully observing who was the leader.

Suddenly, Chen Guiliang placed the other *Sanguosha* boxes on the ground, grabbed one set, and strode forward with a smile, extending his hand in greeting. "Hello, shixiong!"

This shixiong was a little bewildered, shaking Chen Guiliang's hand instinctively. "Hello."

Chen Guiliang said, "Your badminton training is excellent, practically at a professional level. I've loved playing badminton since I was a child, and I really admire athletic people like you."

The shixiong, whose name was unknown, was embarrassed by the compliment. "We're not really professionals, let alone great athletes. We're just a little better than amateurs. Shidi, if you like playing badminton, you can join our training. Although the badminton association's registration period is over, you can practice with us first and join during the next recruitment."

Chen Guiliang, with his 1.8-meter frame, said, "I can't. I've been frail since I was young. At most, I can help you with logistics."

The shixiong said, "If you're frail, you should exercise more. I think shidi has a good foundation."

"Alright, I'll exercise more in the future," Chen Guiliang said, presenting the already opened box of *Sanguosha*. "I saw that you shixiong and your fellow students were training very hard, so I brought a gift for you to relax with. When you're too tired from training in the future, you can play some cards to unwind."

"A gift?" The shixiong couldn't figure out what Chen Guiliang was up to.

Chen Guiliang gazed at the shixiong with incredibly clear eyes and said in an incredibly sincere tone, "Yes, you all train so hard, it moved me very, very much, so I decided to give you a gift."

A complete stranger, giving him a gift for no reason?

The shixiong was completely baffled. He took the box of *Sanguosha* and said, "Then... thank you, shidi?"

"You're welcome. We're all badminton lovers, we're family," Chen Guiliang opened the box, took out the cards, and said, "This gift is a type of card game. I was afraid you might not know how to play, so I'll teach you right now."

"Stop, stop, stop!"

The shixiong quickly stopped him. "I still have to supervise the technical training here."

"My apologies, that was presumptuous of me," Chen Guiliang seemed to have just realized, then pointed to the students resting on the side. "It seems like they take breaks in turns, right? How about this, I'll teach them how to play first, and then have them teach you, shixiong."

"No, what exactly are you doing here?" The shixiong's head was full of questions.

Chen Guiliang took out his business card and student ID. "I'm Chen Guiliang, a freshman from the Yuanpei Program, and also the founder of Game Science and ByteDance. My two companies have already been admitted into the Peking University Science Park as officially supported incubation projects. I personally have a great passion for the sport of badminton. If I make money in the future, I will definitely sponsor the badminton association every year!"

The shixiong took the business card and looked at it carefully, then glanced at Chen Guiliang's student ID. "You started two companies as a freshman, and they're both incubation projects?"

"Absolutely true," Chen Guiliang said with a pained expression. "Starting a business isn't easy. I'm a kid from the countryside. The money I used to start my companies came from author's fees I earned through hard work. If the projects don't work out, it will all go down the drain."

The shixiong asked tentatively, "So, you're here to promote your product?"

"A gift," Chen Guiliang said with a serious expression. "I'm not charging a single cent. This is a gift for the badminton association. As long as it can bring joy to all you badminton aces, I'll consider it my own small contribution to the cause of Chinese badminton."

The shixiong was at a loss for whether to laugh or cry.

This is just a badminton club. What are you talking about, the cause of Chinese badminton?

But his words were so beautifully put that the shixiong even felt a little smug. In any case, he didn't have to pay for anything, and maybe he really could get sponsorship in the future. The shixiong pointed at a few resting members. "Go talk to them."

"Thank you, shixiong, for fulfilling my childhood dream of contributing to the cause of Chinese badminton!" Chen Guiliang shook his hand enthusiastically again.

The shixiong, feeling puffed up, straightened his back and said to the members in training, "Very good, let's continue with our technical drills and fully display the prowess of our badminton athletes!"

Chen Guiliang, carrying the box of *Sanguosha*, walked over to the students who were resting. "Hello, everyone. I've created a card game based on the Three Kingdoms theme. Since you're all on a break anyway, why not play a couple of rounds for fun?"

Ten minutes later...

"Hua Tuo, where's your Peach? Save me! If the Spy dies, how are you going to take on the Monarch alone?"

"I have two black cards left."

"Hey, no table talk."

"Forget it, I give up. Monarch, can you not pick Sun Quan next time?"

"Hahaha, again, again, this *Sanguosha* is so much fun."

The card game on the sidelines grew livelier and livelier, and from time to time, members in training would get distracted and glance over.

The shixiong was a little annoyed. He turned to tell Chen Guiliang to keep it down, only to find no one there.

"Where did he go?" the shixiong asked.

A club member who was playing cards weakly pointed toward the basketball court next to them.

The shixiong looked in that direction and saw Chen Guiliang, holding another box of *Sanguosha*, enthusiastically conversing with the people playing basketball there.

Chen Guiliang had loved basketball since he was a child. He, too, wanted to do his part for the development of Chinese basketball.

Second Teaching Building, Classroom 203.

A senior, an experienced mountaineer, was giving a lecture to the new members of the Shanying Mountaineering Club. "Why do we make you run several kilometers two or three times a week? Why do we practice various technical maneuvers? Because it can save your life in a critical moment!"

"In 1999, the Shanying Club experienced its first mountaineering accident since its founding. The student who died lost her balance, slid all the way down the mountain, and ultimately fell off a cliff, tragically losing her life. She could have performed evasive maneuvers to avoid the tragedy, but she had no stamina left..."

"Especially two years ago, when five members tragically died, we have become even more cautious since then. For every mountaineering activity, we must hold a review meeting in advance, inviting school leaders, old members, and professionals from the Chinese Mountaineering Association to assess it..."

"I know some new members are already getting impatient, complaining that we haven't organized a single mountaineering trip in the two months since they joined. This is for your own safety..."

The lecture lasted a full forty minutes, finally managing to calm down the new members who were clamoring to go mountaineering.

The Shanying Club was Peking University's largest club, with its membership numbers exceeding the second-largest by a landslide.

Chen Guiliang had given them two sets of *Sanguosha*.

Two days ago, the head of logistics and the head of external relations had both had barbecue with Chen Guiliang. Chen Guiliang had also promised to sponsor professional mountaineering equipment next year.

And his only request was for everyone to play some *Sanguosha*.

After seeing off the senior member who had given the lecture, the head of logistics took out a box of *Sanguosha* and said, "I recently discovered something interesting, pretty good for killing time. Those who have urgent matters can leave first. Those who are free this weekend, come play cards with me."

Twenty minutes later, someone watching them play got anxious. "Who wants to switch with me for a couple of rounds?"

"Haha, I'm changing the judgment to a Three of Spades, lightning strikes you dead."

"Peach, peach, peach, I need a peach."

"It should be my turn next round, right?"

"Go buy your own set. There's a sticker on the box with handwritten addresses for on- and off-campus purchasing."

"Why didn't you say so earlier!"

Chen Guiliang had already gone to all the shops on and off campus, big and small, that sold cultural and sports goods.

He offered a 20-25% commission. If they agreed, he would leave a few boxes—he couldn't leave too many, as the shops were reluctant. The boxes took up space, and it was uncertain how well they would sell.

If a shop sold out, they would call him for a restock.

By the side of Weiming Lake.

The 2004 Yuanpei Program students were holding their first all-class gathering after the start of classes.

There was no fixed agenda. It was just to let everyone get together, so they wouldn't be strangers to each other.

They could chat about anything.

By their sophomore and junior years, there would even be small circles dedicated to academic discussions.

Chen Guiliang came speeding over on his second bicycle.

He had really put five locks on it. This certainly wouldn't stop a thief, but it would increase the difficulty of stealing it. When a whole row of bicycles was parked there, a thief would surely choose the one that was easiest to steal.

It was like in ancient times, when an army was defeated. A deserter didn't necessarily have to outrun the pursuers, just be faster than his own comrades.

"Chen Guiliang, hurry up, why are you so late!"

A few classmates he was more familiar with called out.

The fourteen junior-year teaching assistants were also there. Chen Guiliang dropped his bike and ran over, carrying a box of *Sanguosha*.

After about ten more minutes, everyone had arrived.

The teaching assistants encouraged everyone to stand up and share their experiences and what they had gained during this period. Because aside from the members of their own small groups, the other students in the class were still very unfamiliar with each other.

Under these circumstances, there wasn't much to talk about between groups. They had to talk about themselves to break the ice.

"Let me say a few words." Chen Guiliang stood up.

"Alright, let's welcome student Chen Guiliang to share his exciting life during this period!"

But Chen Guiliang pulled out a stack of business cards. Each of the 14 teaching assistants and over 140 students would get one.

As Chen Guiliang handed out the cards, he said, "I used my author's fees to start two companies, which have successfully passed the review for the Peking University Science Park's incubation program and already have office space in the Science Park. The *Sanguosha* I brought today is one of my projects. I plan to donate two sets of *Sanguosha* to our Yuanpei Program, so we can play anytime during future class activities..."

The 14 teaching assistants: "..."

The 140-plus students: "..."

Everyone looked at each other. Apart from those in the same dorm room and small group as Chen Guiliang, and a few from the rooms across and next door, this was the first time the other students learned he had started companies.

Finally, a girl exclaimed, "Chen Guiliang, you're so amazing. How long have you been at Peking University, and you've already started two companies."

"Yeah, he's a big boss without making a sound," another boy chimed in.

Chen Guiliang said with a pained expression, "What money am I making? My past author's fees, the prize money for getting into Peking University, I've poured it all into the companies. I even got a 100,000 yuan advance on my royalties from my publisher, and when I invested it, it barely made a splash. That's an investment of over two hundred thousand yuan, and I haven't even earned back a fraction of it. If my projects fail, not only will I lose everything, but I'll also be in debt to my publisher for one hundred thousand yuan!"

Upon hearing this, the crowd was even more shocked.

An investment of over two hundred thousand yuan was an astronomical sum for a student.

Some even felt a sense of pity for Chen Guiliang. If his business failed, that was over two hundred thousand yuan!

The fourteen junior-year teaching assistants, however, had different thoughts. The way they looked at Chen Guiliang changed.

Chen Guiliang waved to the teaching assistants. "Shixiong, shijie, come over and play *Sanguosha*. We can chat and have our class exchange while we play."

Finally, the fourth update is done. I'm almost written out. Pleading for support.
